proof_steps.comparison: Hopf groups have finite-index Z and Kodaira groups a finite-index two-step nilpotent lattice. The printed properly elliptic route uses the canonical bundle formula with χ(O)=0: K is the pullback of the orbifold canonical divisor plus a degree-zero line bundle. Kodaira dimension1 forces positive orbifold degree; a degree-zero line bundle on a compact curve has at most one section in each power, so cannot have dimension1. The hyperbolic orbifold group has a finite-index genus≥2 surface group, hence is not solvable. The orbifold quotient map therefore rules out that case. The frozen proof independently excludes every elliptic option via the exact orbifold sequence, cohomological dimension4 and the finite-cover central extension over an elliptic base. At b2=0, the cited class-VII classification leaves Inoue; the already proved extension contradicts b1(Y)=0.

exact_character_form_transport: On a local universal-cover chart the pullback of the printed form is d log Im(w). For a loop whose lifted endpoint is (aw+b,...) its integral is log Im(aw+b)−log Im(w)=log a. Thus the de Rham period homomorphism of θ is exactly the frozen slope character χ, not merely a proportional nonzero class. Abelianization and UCT send that same homomorphism to the global H1-cohomology class, and naturality identifies fibre restrictions. The meridian estimate applies to the actual map of the transverse disc into Y; a local base equation u(z)z^m sends its meridian to m base turns, but no replacement by one turn enters either proof.

The cyclic-extension H1 calculation therefore gives b1(H)=1; the finite cover has Euler characteristic0, so b2=0. It is minimal and its group remains solvable, not virtually nilpotent. A differentiable marking over a base disc transports the finite-index subgroup and constructs a finite covering of the whole family; pull back the complex charts to obtain a holomorphic cover. Taking the core gives a finite Galois cover. Its quotient deck transformations normalize that core's first-coordinate group, which still contains a nonzero translation and dilation, so the same unique-fixed-point argument forces positive-real affine first coordinates. Consequently the form descends and its pullback has nonzero logα period. A zero downstairs class would pull back to zero, so the quotient class is nonzero.
